1:
\textbf{(a)} Separate: $e^{y-1}dy=\sin(4x)\,dx\Rightarrow e^{y-1}=-\frac{\cos4x}{4}+C$. $y(0)=1$: $1=-\frac14+C$, so $C=\frac54$:
\[\boxed{y=1+\ln\Big(\frac{5-\cos4x}{4}\Big)}.\]
\textbf{(b)} $y'+\big(\frac1t+2\big)y=\frac{12}{t}$. Integrating factor $e^{\ln t+2t}=te^{2t}$:
\[(te^{2t}y)'=12e^{2t}\ \Rightarrow\ te^{2t}y=6e^{2t}+C\ \Rightarrow\ \boxed{y=\frac6t+\frac{Ce^{-2t}}{t}}.\]
2:
\textbf{(a)} $y'=e^x+r+2sx$, $y''=e^x+2s$, so $y''-y'=(2s-r)-2sx=8x+10$. Then $-2s=8$ and $2s-r=10$: \boxed{r=-18,\ s=-4}.

\textbf{(b)} i. Equilibria: $y=0,8,10$. Sign of $f=y(10-y)(y-8)^2$: negative for $y<0$, positive on $(0,8)$ and $(8,10)$, negative for $y>10$.
\[y=0:\ \textbf{unstable};\quad y=8:\ \textbf{semistable};\quad y=10:\ \textbf{stable}.\]
ii. Starting at 9 (between 8 and 10, $f>0$), the solution rises to the stable equilibrium: $\lim_{t\to\infty}y(t)=\boxed{10}$.
4:
\textbf{(a)} $f(t,y)=2y^2-6t$, $h=\frac12$. Step 1: $f(0,1)=2$, so $y(0.5)\approx1+\frac12(2)=2$. Step 2: $f(0.5,2)=8-3=5$, so $y(1)\approx2+\frac12(5)=\boxed{4.5}$.

\textbf{(b)} i. \boxed{\dfrac{dB}{dt}=0.03B-K,\quad B(0)=100{,}000}.

ii. The equilibrium is $B=\frac{K}{0.03}$, and it is unstable: the balance grows if it starts above it. So the balance increases when $100{,}000>\frac{K}{0.03}$, i.e. \boxed{K<3000\ \text{dollars per year}}.
5:
\textbf{(a)} Volume $V(t)=100+30t$. Salt in: $5\cdot50=250$ g/min; out: $20\cdot\frac{y}{100+30t}$:
\[\boxed{\frac{dy}{dt}=250-\frac{20y}{100+30t},\quad y(0)=20}.\]
\textbf{(b)} $V=x^3$ and surface area $6x^2=6V^{2/3}$:
\[\boxed{\frac{dV}{dt}=-1.2\,V^{2/3},\quad V(0)=1000}.\]
